pages.subtitle: On a snowy night during a war, Mary appeared in the sky over a small French village with a message of hope.

quick_facts.label: Church says
quick_facts.value: Approved by the local bishop in 1872

pages.intro: In January 1871, France was at war, and the enemy army was coming closer. In the small village of Pontmain, the families were afraid. Their young men had gone to fight, and no one had heard from them. Then, one snowy evening, four children saw a beautiful lady in the night sky. Words in gold letters appeared beneath her: "But pray, my children."
story_paragraphs: In the winter of 1871, France was fighting a war against Prussia. Thirty-eight young men from the village of Pontmain had gone off to war, and their families had heard nothing from them for months. A sickness was spreading too. The enemy army was getting close.

On the evening of January 17, a twelve-year-old boy named Eugène Barbedette stepped outside his family's barn. He looked up at the starry sky. There, above a neighbor's house, he saw a beautiful lady smiling at him. She wore a blue dress covered with golden stars, a black veil, and a golden crown.

Eugène's younger brother, Joseph, saw her too. Their parents saw nothing. Soon two girls from the village school, Françoise Richer and Jeanne-Marie Lebossé, came and saw the lady as well. The grown-ups could not see her, but they believed the children. A sister from the school led everyone in praying the Rosary.

As the villagers prayed, the children watched. A white banner slowly unrolled beneath the lady's feet. Gold letters appeared on it, one by one: "But pray, my children. God will answer you very soon. My Son allows himself to be touched." Later, the lady held a red cross. Her face was sad, but she did not cry. At last, a white veil rose up and covered her, and she was gone.

That same evening, the enemy army stopped its advance. The soldiers did not come into the region, and a few days later a peace agreement was signed. All thirty-eight young men of Pontmain came home safely.
A year later, the bishop declared that Mary had truly appeared. A large church was built in Pontmain, and people began to call Mary there "Our Lady of Hope."

pages.subtitle: Mary appeared to two Polish girls and spoke to them in their own language, when that language was being forbidden.

quick_facts.label: Church says
quick_facts.value: Approved by the local bishop in 1977

pages.intro: In 1877, two girls in a Polish village saw Mary sitting near a maple tree by their church. Mary spoke to them in Polish, the language their families spoke at home. At that time, the government was trying to stop people from using Polish in school. Mary asked everyone to pray the Rosary every day. Gietrzwałd is the only place in Poland where the Church has approved an apparition of Mary.
story_paragraphs: In 1877, the village of Gietrzwałd was part of Prussia, a German country. Poland did not exist as its own country then. The government wanted everyone to speak German, and it had forbidden Polish in schools. It was also making life hard for the Catholic Church. Many parishes had no priests.

On June 27, 1877, a thirteen-year-old girl named Justyna Szafryńska was walking home from a test she had taken before her First Communion. Near the church, she saw a lady dressed in white, shining with light.

Three days later, a twelve-year-old girl named Barbara Samulowska was praying the Rosary with Justyna. She saw the lady too. The lady was sitting on a throne at the foot of a maple tree in front of the church. Angels were around her, and she held the child Jesus on her knee.

The girls asked the lady who she was. She answered in Polish, "I am the Most Blessed Virgin Mary, the Immaculate Conception." When they asked what she wanted, she said she wanted them to pray the Rosary every day.

The girls also asked about their Church and about the parishes that had no priests. Mary said that if people prayed with all their hearts, the Church would not be persecuted, and the parishes would have priests again.

Mary appeared to the girls many times that summer. On the last day, September 16, she blessed a spring of water near the village. Pilgrims came from all over, even though the government fined some of them.
One hundred years later, in 1977, the bishop declared that the apparitions were real. Barbara grew up to be a religious sister. She spent most of her life serving the poor in Guatemala.

pages.subtitle: In Lithuania, Mary was seen weeping where a church had once stood, and a lost treasure was found.

quick_facts.label: Who saw her
quick_facts.value: Children from the village, then many villagers

quick_facts.label: Church says
quick_facts.value: Devotion approved by Pope Pius VI in 1775

pages.intro: In 1608, children watching sheep near the village of Šiluva in Lithuania saw a beautiful lady holding a baby. She was weeping. She stood on the very spot where a Catholic church had stood before it was taken away and destroyed. Her tears led the people to find a buried treasure: an old painting of Mary and the papers that proved the land belonged to the church.
story_paragraphs: Long ago, in the village of Šiluva, in Lithuania, there was a Catholic church with a painting of Mary holding the child Jesus. People came from far away to pray there.

In the 1500s, many people in the area left the Catholic Church and became Protestants called Calvinists. The church in Šiluva was taken away and later burned down. Before it was lost, the last priest hid the painting of Mary and the church's important papers in a strong chest. He buried it in the ground near a large rock.
Many years passed. People forgot where the chest was hidden.
Then, in 1608, some children were watching their sheep at the edge of the village. They saw a beautiful lady standing on a rock, holding a baby in her arms. She was weeping bitterly.

The next day, many villagers came to see. A Calvinist teacher came too, and he asked her why she was crying. The old account says she answered that her Son had once been worshipped on this very spot, and now people plowed and planted there instead.

Then, the story says, an old blind man who had helped bury the chest long ago came to the field. There, he could see again. He pointed to the place where the chest was buried. The people dug, and they found the painting and the papers, still safe.

With those papers, the Catholics of Šiluva got their church land back. A new church was built, and the painting was placed in it. In 1775, Pope Pius VI approved the devotion. Today, a great church stands in Šiluva, and it is the largest place of pilgrimage to Mary in Lithuania.

pages.subtitle: In a small convent in Japan, a sister heard Mary's voice, and a wooden statue of Mary was seen to weep.

quick_facts.label: When
quick_facts.value: 1973, with the statue weeping from 1975 to 1981

quick_facts.label: Church says
quick_facts.value: The local bishop recognized the events in 1984

pages.intro: In 1973, in a small convent near the city of Akita, Japan, a sister named Agnes Sasagawa heard a voice coming from a wooden statue of Mary. The voice asked for prayer, especially the Rosary, and prayer for the Pope, bishops, and priests. Later, the statue was seen to weep, again and again, for six years. The local bishop studied it carefully and saw the tears himself.
story_paragraphs: Agnes Sasagawa grew up in Japan as a Buddhist. She became a Catholic as a young woman. She was often sick. Just a few months before she joined a small community of sisters near Akita, she lost her hearing and became completely deaf.
The sisters belonged to a community called the Handmaids of the Eucharist. In their chapel stood a wooden statue of Mary, about three feet tall, carved from a single block of wood.
In the summer of 1973, Sister Agnes was praying in the chapel. She heard a gentle voice coming from the statue. It was Mary. Mary spoke to her three times that year, in July, August, and October.

Mary asked Sister Agnes and the other sisters to pray. She asked them to pray the Rosary often, and to pray for the Pope, the bishops, and the priests. She also told Agnes that her deafness would be healed. Some of Mary's words were serious. She asked people to turn back to God and to make sacrifices for others.

Then something even more surprising happened. Starting in January 1975, the wooden statue began to shed tears. It wept on and off for more than six years, 101 times in all. The sisters saw it, and hundreds of visitors saw it too. It was even shown on Japanese television.

The bishop of the area, John Shojiro Ito, saw the tears with his own eyes. Scientists at a university studied them. In 1984, after eight years of study, the bishop recognized that the events were supernatural.
Sister Agnes lived quietly with her community for many years. She died on August 15, 2024, the feast of the Assumption of Mary, at age 93.

pages.subtitle: On a farm in Venezuela, Mary came as the Reconciler of all peoples, and many people saw her at once.

quick_facts.label: Who saw her
quick_facts.value: Maria Esperanza de Bianchini, and later many pilgrims

quick_facts.label: Church says
quick_facts.value: Approved by the local bishop in 1987

pages.intro: On a farm called Betania in Venezuela, a mother named Maria Esperanza saw Mary beside a waterfall in 1976. Mary called herself the Reconciler of all peoples and nations. She came to help people make peace with God and with one another. In 1984, more than a hundred people saw Mary at the same time. The local bishop studied it carefully and approved it.
story_paragraphs: Maria Esperanza was born in Venezuela in 1928. From the time she was a little girl, she loved God very much. She married a man named Geo Bianchini, and they had seven children.
Maria and her family had a farm in the hills of Venezuela called Betania. On the farm there was a grotto with a waterfall.

On March 25, 1976, the feast of the Annunciation, Maria Esperanza was at the grotto when she saw the Virgin Mary. Mary called herself "Mary, Virgin and Mother, Reconciler of all Peoples and Nations." To reconcile means to bring people back together in peace. Mary came to help people make peace with God and with one another.

Mary appeared to Maria several more times. Then something special happened. On March 25, 1984, a large group of pilgrims was praying at the farm. That afternoon, about 108 people saw Mary appear near the waterfall. Many of them were ordinary families, and some had come out of curiosity.

The bishop of the area, Pío Bello Ricardo, began a careful study. He talked with hundreds of people who said they had seen Mary. In 1987, he wrote that the apparitions "are authentic and have a supernatural character," and he approved them. He also allowed a chapel to be built at Betania.

Maria Esperanza spent the rest of her life helping people come closer to God. She said the biggest problem in the world was the division between people. She died in 2004 in New Jersey. The Church has opened her cause for sainthood, so she is now called a Servant of God.

pages.subtitle: In a small town in Nicaragua, Mary asked a church caretaker to pray the Rosary and to tell people to love and forgive.

quick_facts.label: Church says
quick_facts.value: The local bishop allowed the account to be published

pages.intro: In 1980, Nicaragua was a country full of fighting and fear. In the small town of Cuapa, a man named Bernardo Martínez took care of the church. One day, he saw a lady dressed in white standing on a cloud. She said, "I come from heaven. I am the Mother of Jesus." She asked people to pray the Rosary, to love one another, and to forgive.
story_paragraphs: Cuapa is a small farming town in Nicaragua, in Central America. In 1980, Nicaragua had just been through a war, and many people were angry and afraid.

Bernardo Martínez was a farmer in Cuapa. He was also the sacristan of the town's little church. A sacristan takes care of the church and gets things ready for Mass. In April 1980, Bernardo noticed that a statue of Mary in the church was glowing with light, all by itself.

A few weeks later, on May 8, Bernardo was down by a river near the town. Suddenly, he saw a lady standing on a bright white cloud. She wore a white dress and a cream-colored veil, and her feet were bare. She looked like the statue of Our Lady of Fatima.

The lady said, "I come from heaven. I am the Mother of Jesus." She told Bernardo, "I want you to pray the Rosary every day." She also said, "I want you to love one another." She asked people to make peace and not to ask God for peace without making peace themselves.

Mary appeared to Bernardo several more times that year. On October 13, 1980, about fifty people came with Bernardo to pray. They saw a circle of light on the ground, and Bernardo saw Mary again. She asked everyone to "forgive one another."
Bernardo told the bishop everything. The bishop allowed Bernardo's account to be printed so that others could read it, and many people began to come to Cuapa to pray.
Later, Bernardo felt God calling him to be a priest. On August 20, 1995, when he was 63 years old, Bernardo was ordained a priest.

pages.student_title: Our Lady of the Rosary of San Nicolás
pages.subtitle: In Argentina, Mary led a grandmother to a forgotten statue and asked for a shrine where people could come to pray.

quick_facts.label: Where
quick_facts.value: San Nicolás de los Arroyos, Argentina

quick_facts.label: Church says
quick_facts.value: Approved by the local bishop in 2016

pages.intro: In 1983, rosaries in several homes in the city of San Nicolás, Argentina, began to glow. Then a grandmother named Gladys Motta saw Mary, dressed in blue and holding the baby Jesus. Mary asked her to find a forgotten statue and to have a shrine built. In 2016, the local bishop recognized that the events were supernatural. Today, huge crowds of pilgrims come there to pray.
story_paragraphs: San Nicolás de los Arroyos is a city in Argentina, in South America. In 1983, Gladys Quiroga de Motta lived there. She was a wife, a mother of two daughters, and a grandmother. She had only gone to school for a few years.
That year, something strange began to happen in her city. In several homes, rosaries started to glow with light.

On September 25, 1983, Gladys saw Mary for the first time. Mary wore a blue gown and veil, and she held the baby Jesus in her arms. About a month later, Mary gave Gladys a white rosary and said, "Receive this Rosary from my hands."

Mary asked Gladys to find an old statue of her. The statue had been blessed by Pope Leo XIII and brought all the way from Rome, but it had been damaged and forgotten. On November 27, 1983, Gladys found it, hidden away in the bell tower of the cathedral. It looked just like the lady she had seen.
Mary also asked for a shrine to be built, a special church where people could come to pray. The bishop agreed, and work began in 1987. The statue was placed inside.
Over the years, Gladys received many messages. Mary asked people to pray, to turn back to God, and to go to the sacraments. Every year on May 22, crowds of pilgrims walk to the shrine to pray.

On May 22, 2016, at the end of the yearly pilgrimage Mass, Bishop Héctor Cardelli announced that he recognized "the supernatural nature" of the events. Gladys has lived quietly and has always obeyed the bishops.

pages.subtitle: In a convent in Quito, Ecuador, a nun told of seeing Mary, and a beloved statue of Mary was made.

quick_facts.label: Church says
quick_facts.value: Devotion to the statue is approved; the apparitions are not formally approved

pages.intro: Long ago, a girl named Mariana sailed from Spain to Quito, in South America, to help start a convent of sisters. She became the leader of the convent. According to tradition, Mary appeared to her and asked for a statue to be made. That statue, Our Lady of Good Success, has been loved in Quito for more than 400 years. The Church is still studying Mother Mariana's life.
story_paragraphs: Mariana de Jesús Torres was born in Spain in 1563. When she was about thirteen years old, she sailed across the ocean with a small group of sisters. They went to Quito, a city high in the mountains of what is now Ecuador. There they started the first convent in the city.
Mariana grew up in the convent and became a sister herself. Later, she became the abbess, the leader of the sisters.

The story of what happened next comes to us from people who loved Mother Mariana and wrote about her. They say that on February 2, 1594, Mary appeared to her. Mary held the child Jesus in her right arm. In her other hand, she held a staff, like the one an abbess carries, and the keys of the convent.

According to the story, Mary asked Mother Mariana to have a statue made of her, just as she appeared. Mary wanted the statue placed above the abbess's chair, as a sign that she was the true leader and protector of the convent.

A sculptor named Francisco del Castillo carved the statue. On February 2, 1611, the bishop of Quito blessed it. The statue was given the name Our Lady of Good Success. It still stands in the convent today.
Mother Mariana died on January 16, 1635. The sisters have honored her ever since.

In 1986, the Church opened a study of Mother Mariana's life, to see if she might one day be named a saint. In 1991, the archbishop made the convent a sanctuary of Mary for the whole city, and people still come to pray before the statue.
